No. At that moment the Moon would be far below Perth’s horizon, at an altitude of about **−51.9°**. That means it is roughly 52 degrees beneath the horizon in the direction of azimuth **276°** (almost due west), so terrain or atmospheric conditions are irrelevant—it is geometrically not visible from your location.

Although the Moon is only a thin **5.75% crescent**, which would make it challenging even if above the horizon, its altitude is the decisive factor here. You would need to wait until it rises later, likely in the pre-dawn hours.
